project.title: Cross-Sector Digital Intake and Case-Handling Standardisation
project.objective: Design and pilot a unified digital intake and case-handling workflow for health, education, courts and civil service units to reduce errors and improve processing times.
deliverables: Current-state process maps for medical, education, court and civil service intake
Unified intake and case-handling workflow and standard operating procedures
Standardised digital forms and document templates for all sectors
Data handling and confidentiality guidelines aligned with legal requirements
Pilot implementation report with metrics and improvement recommendations
constraints: Must comply with sector-specific legislation and data protection rules
No changes to core case management systems, only workflows and templates
Standard forms must be usable by staff with basic office software skills
Pilot must be scoped to a limited number of case types per sector
All documentation must be auditable and version-controlled

risks.risk: Sector teams resist changing familiar intake procedures.
risks.mitigation: Involve representatives from each sector in design workshops and collect feedback through structured reviews.

risks.risk: New templates fail to meet legal or policy requirements.
risks.mitigation: Have court and civil service officers review all templates against legislation before approval.

risks.risk: Digital forms are too complex for frontline staff to adopt quickly.
risks.mitigation: Run short training sessions, provide quick-reference guides and iterate based on pilot feedback.

risks.risk: Inconsistent application of confidentiality rules across sectors.
risks.mitigation: Create shared confidentiality guidelines and include explicit checks in the workflow and training materials.

themes.why_relevant: Core to reducing rework and ensuring consistent data capture across all sectors.
Court, health, education and civil service processes must all meet strict legal requirements.
Sensitive personal data is handled in all sectors and must be protected in the new workflow.
Multiple administrative units must align on shared procedures and responsibilities.
Staff need clear guidance and support to adopt new workflows and templates.

backlog.task: Document current medical intake and case-handling workflow
definition_of_done: End-to-end medical intake process mapped with key steps and actors
List of all current medical forms and templates compiled
Pain points and common errors in medical intake documented
Process map and notes stored in shared project folder

backlog.task: Document current education intake and case-handling workflow
definition_of_done: Education intake and case-handling steps described in a process map
Existing education forms and templates catalogued
Policy constraints and approval steps identified
Summary shared with project team for review

backlog.task: Document current court intake and case-handling workflow
definition_of_done: Court intake and registration steps mapped for standard case types
List of mandatory court documents and evidence items compiled
Legal time limits and notification requirements noted
Validated by a second court administrative officer

backlog.task: Document current civil service intake and enquiry handling workflow
definition_of_done: Civil service intake and enquiry routing steps mapped
Existing request forms and channels listed
Escalation rules and transparency requirements captured
Process document uploaded and shared with team

backlog.task: Draft unified intake data model and minimum data set
definition_of_done: Common data fields across sectors identified and defined
Sector-specific mandatory fields listed separately
Draft data model reviewed by medical and court representatives
Final version approved for template design

backlog.task: Design standardised digital intake form for medical cases
definition_of_done: Form created in agreed office software format
Fields aligned with unified data model and medical needs
Confidentiality and consent sections included
Form tested with at least two sample cases and adjusted

backlog.task: Design standardised digital intake form for court cases
definition_of_done: Court intake form drafted with mandatory legal fields
Sections for evidence and deadlines clearly structured
Reviewed against court procedures and civil process order
Approved by another court administrative officer

backlog.task: Draft cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline
definition_of_done: Key confidentiality rules from all sectors summarised
Access control and document sharing practices defined
Guideline reviewed by court and medical representatives
Version-controlled document shared with all stakeholders

backlog.task: Create unified intake workflow and standard operating procedure
definition_of_done: Step-by-step workflow covering all sectors documented
Roles and responsibilities for each step clarified
Linked to relevant forms and confidentiality guideline
SOP approved by representatives from all sectors

backlog.task: Prepare quick-reference checklists for frontline staff
definition_of_done: One-page checklists drafted for each sector
Includes key steps, required documents and checks
Reviewed by at least one officer from each sector
Uploaded to shared folder and referenced in SOP

backlog.task: Plan and coordinate pilot implementation across sectors
definition_of_done: Pilot scope and case types agreed with all stakeholders
Timeline and responsibilities documented
Communication sent to participating staff
Pilot tracking sheet prepared for feedback and metrics

backlog.task: Consolidate pilot feedback and propose improvements
definition_of_done: Feedback from all sectors collected and summarised
Issues grouped by process, template and training
Concrete improvement proposals listed and prioritised
Pilot report shared and validated by project team

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on scope, sectors, and case types for the standardisation project.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message announcing the project and asking for confirmation of scope and priorities.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on which case types per sector will be included in the first standardisation wave.
Confirm overall project timeline and key milestones for the 30-day window.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review and finalise the unified intake data model and standard forms.
threads_plan.trigger: Education policy officer shares draft unified data model and requests feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the unified intake data model and minimum data set for all sectors.
Sign off on sector-specific digital intake form templates for pilot use.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Agree on confidentiality rules and how they apply in the new workflow.
threads_plan.trigger: Civil service administrative officer posts draft confidentiality guideline for comments.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Validate the unified intake workflow, SOP, and frontline checklists.
threads_plan.trigger: Education policy officer shares draft SOP and asks sector reps to test it with sample cases.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the unified intake workflow and SOP for pilot implementation.
Agree on final versions of frontline checklists for each sector.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Plan the pilot, track issues, and agree on improvement actions.
threads_plan.trigger: Civil service administrative officer opens discussion on pilot scope, schedule, and tracking.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm pilot scope, tracking approach, and criteria for success.

channel_rituals: Twice-weekly async check-in where each participant posts progress on their assigned tasks and blockers.
Weekly review thread to validate drafts of forms, guidelines, and SOPs before sign-off.
Pilot daily log summary during the pilot period capturing issues and quick fixes.
End-of-project retrospective thread to capture lessons learned and follow-up actions.
